title: Patchwork surveys: random rectangles of every training view are replaced by the SAME ground from another survey (or, sometimes, by unrelated ground), so a place must be recognised from whatever survives local change
hypothesis: Champion exp 20 (0.0777) on held-out truedop_2024: usable 93.0%, false fix 0.75% (3 frames), abstain 6.25% (25 frames); the three training photographs score 100% usable / 0% false at the same held-out viewpoints, so the whole remaining score is the survey gap, and it is mostly abstention. Every survey-invariance mechanism this era has kept or tried acts on the WHOLE frame at once: photometric/blur nuisance (exp 4), MixStyle feature statistics (exp 14), weight averaging (exp 20), JS consistency of beliefs across surveys (exp 23, reverted), and the pretrained trunks (exps 12-19). None of them touches what actually differs LOCALLY between two surveys of the same ground: one block's trees are in leaf in one capture and bare in another, a courtyard is in shadow in one and lit in the next, a car park is full or empty, a construction site has moved on. A GAP-pooled place descriptor trained on three captures can lean on whichever few distinctive patches all three happen to agree on; when one of those patches differs in 2024, the descriptor moves off its prototype, the committee members' mass spreads, and the frame abstains (or, rarely, lands confidently elsewhere). The four captures are registered to one grid within 1 px, so the training set already contains the exact local substitutions a fourth survey makes: the same pixels of ground as photographed by another survey. Pasting rectangles of another training survey into a view, at the same ground position and heading, manufactures a new 'survey' per view whose season, shadow and contents vary REGION BY REGION, a combinatorial family the three whole photographs never show. A smaller share of rectangles filled with unrelated ground (another position in the batch) stands in for change that no training survey contains (new buildings, demolition). The training signal is then: the label stays put while any ~10-40% of the frame changes, so the descriptor must spread its evidence across the frame's stable structure instead of a few fingerprint patches. Builds on exp 6 (pixel blending of whole surveys, reverted on the from-scratch trunk of that time) by making the mixing spatial and local rather than a global alpha blend, and on exp 14's insight that cross-survey mixing helps, carried from feature statistics to content. Plateau note: exps 21-26 were four reverts of training-procedure and trunk-weight variations; this changes a stage never questioned in the era, the CONTENT of the training views (only their photometry, sharpness and heading have ever been randomised).
method: model/train.py only. New function survey_patchwork(x, alt, foreign) applied per member, per batch, in run_epoch: with probability PATCH_P = 0.6 per view, draw PATCH_K = 3 axis-aligned rectangles (each independently active with prob 0.7; side lengths uniform in [12, 48] px, centres uniform over the 128 px frame, clipped to it). Each active rectangle takes its pixels from `alt` (the same position, same heading, a DIFFERENT training capture, cut by one extra gpu_crops call per batch) with prob 0.75, else from `foreign` (the batch's own clean crops under a random permutation, i.e. other ground). Applied to the clean crop before augment_views, so photometric nuisance acts on the composite as a whole. Labels, targets, loss, model, decode and export are unchanged. BN recalibration of the averaged model is left as it is (no patchwork), so the exported statistics match whole, unedited frames.
expected_outcome: mission_score 0.078 -> ~0.05-0.06 on truedop_2024, mainly through abstention: abstain 6.25% -> ~4%, usable 93.0% -> ~95%, false fix stays <= 1.0% (the committee's min-mass confidence is untouched; foreign-ground rectangles teach that unfamiliar content is not evidence for any place, which if anything sharpens honesty). Training-capture diagnostics stay ~0.000 (100% usable): the edit removes nothing from clean frames, which are still 40% of views. Training top1 on augmented views reads a few points lower by design. If 2024 usable does NOT move while training diagnostics hold, local content change is not what separates the surveys and the gap is global (geometry/scale/sensor), which narrows the search. Wall-clock: +1 gpu_crops per batch and cheap masking, ~+5% over the champion's ~110 min.
eli5: We teach the model Berlin from three aerial photographs taken in different years, then test it on a fourth it has never seen. Between photographs, little pieces of the city change: trees gain leaves, shadows move, a car park fills up, a building site grows. So while training, we cut random rectangles out of each picture and fill them with the same spot as it looked in another year's photograph, or occasionally with a piece of somewhere else entirely. The model can no longer rely on one or two memorable details; it has to recognise the place from everything around them, which is what it must do when the new photograph has changed a few details of its own.

stages.name: Camera frame
stages.detail: 128×128 px daytime crop, Berlin only; trained on three survey photographs, scored on a fourth it never saw; enlarged in-graph to 224 px

stages.name: Feature extractor
stages.detail: two independent ImageNet-pretrained EfficientNet-B0 trunks (one per committee member), fine-tuned at a tenth of the learning rate, read at two depths (14×14 and 7×7)

stages.name: Place description
stages.detail: each depth squeezed to 56 numbers and averaged over the frame; the two halves joined into one 112-number description, normalised to unit length

stages.name: Tile prototypes
stages.detail: cosine similarity of the description against one learned direction per 128 m map tile (2,970 tiles), per member

stages.name: Committee decode
stages.detail: average the members' beliefs, pick the best 3×3 block of tiles; confidence = the smaller of the two members' own belief in that block; position = belief-weighted block centre plus a small within-tile nudge

stages.name: Patchwork surveys (training only)
stages.detail: in 60% of training views, up to three random rectangles are replaced by the same ground from another year's photograph (or, one time in four, by unrelated ground); the label stays the same, so the place must be recognised from what survives local change

implementation_brief:
Start from the CURRENT model/ (champion exp 20: two-member EfficientNet-B0 committee, effb0_features7.pt, MixStyle, cosine head, SWA-style weight averaging + BN recalibration). Do NOT touch model/model.py at all except, optionally, its docstring (add a short 'PATCHWORK SURVEYS (capture-holdout era, experiment 27)' paragraph saying the change is training-only and the deployed graph is unchanged). Ignore the untracked model/pretrained/effb0ns_features7.pt and port_effb0_ns.py; do not load them. All changes in model/train.py:

1. Constants next to AUG: PATCH_P = 0.6 (per-view probability of any patchwork), PATCH_K = 3 (rectangles per view), PATCH_RECT_P = 0.7 (each rectangle independently active), PATCH_MIN_PX = 12, PATCH_MAX_PX = 48 (side length range, independent for width and height), PATCH_FOREIGN_P = 0.25 (probability an active rectangle is filled from foreign ground instead of the alternate survey).

2. New function survey_patchwork(x, alt, foreign) -> tensor, fully vectorised on the device (CUDA/MPS/CPU), no Python loop over the batch. x, alt, foreign: float [B,3,H,W] in [0,1], same shape. For each view b and each k in range(PATCH_K): active_bk = (rand < PATCH_P per view) & (rand < PATCH_RECT_P per rect); w,h ~ U[PATCH_MIN_PX, PATCH_MAX_PX] (integers, torch.randint); centre cx,cy ~ U[0,W), U[0,H); rectangle = [cx-w//2, cx+w//2) x [cy-h//2, cy+h//2) clipped to the frame; build the boolean mask with broadcast comparisons against torch.arange(W)/arange(H) -> [B,K,H,W]; is_foreign_bk = rand < PATCH_FOREIGN_P. m_alt = any_k(mask & active & ~foreign) and m_for = any_k(mask & active & foreign), each [B,1,H,W] float. Return x*(1-m_alt) + alt*m_alt, then apply out*(1-m_for) + foreign*m_for (foreign wins where both overlap). Hard edges, no feathering.

3. In run_epoch, per mini-batch, after xb0 = gpu_crops(scene, cap_b, cx[idx], cy[idx], ang[idx]):
   - alt_cap = (cap_b + torch.randint(1, n_caps, cap_b.shape, device=cap_b.device)) % n_caps  (always a DIFFERENT training capture; n_caps is 3, guard: if n_caps < 2, alt_cap = cap_b);
   - xb_alt = gpu_crops(scene, alt_cap, cx[idx], cy[idx], ang[idx])  (same ground position, same heading, so it is pixel-registered with xb0);
   - xb_for = xb0[torch.randperm(B, device=xb0.device)]  (other ground in the same batch);
   - inside the member loop, replace `xb_k = augment_views(xb0)` with `xb_k = augment_views(survey_patchwork(xb0, xb_alt, xb_for))`, so each member gets its OWN independent patchwork draw AND its own photometric draw, as today.
   Targets (make_soft_targets, residual_offset_target), loss_fn, optimiser, LR schedule, weight averaging, logging are all unchanged.

4. Do NOT apply patchwork in recalibrate_bn (keep it exactly as today: gpu_crops -> augment_views), nor in survey_diag or any diagnostic. Those must see whole, unedited frames.

5. Record in the final train_info JSON: add key "patchwork": {"p": PATCH_P, "k": PATCH_K, "rect_p": PATCH_RECT_P, "side_px": [PATCH_MIN_PX, PATCH_MAX_PX], "foreign_p": PATCH_FOREIGN_P, "alt_source": "same position+heading, different training capture"}, and append ', survey patchwork (random rectangles from another training capture at the same ground, or from foreign ground; train only)' to the capture_sampling string. Add one line to the startup log naming the patchwork parameters. Update train.py's module docstring with a short paragraph describing the change.

Fixed contracts to preserve: train.py CLI unchanged (python -m model.train --area berlin --out-dir runs/<id> [--epochs N] [--max-crops-per-bucket N], whatever args exist today stay); training reads ONLY buckets(meta, "train") via load_scene — nothing may open the eval capture truedop_2024 in any form; the export is one ONNX per area at <out>/models/<area>.onnx taking a 1x3x128x128 float32 input in [0,1] and returning [[u, v, conf]] with u, v normalised map coords and conf in [0,1] (export_onnx in model/model.py, unchanged); the exported fp32 ONNX must stay <= 32 MiB (the champion is 31.7 MB; this change adds zero parameters, so the size must be unchanged — do not add anything to the model) and host latency <= 250 ms (unchanged graph). Exported model is still the weight-averaged, BN-recalibrated model, exactly as today. Smoke-check locally with a tiny run (e.g. --epochs 1 with max_chunks-style timing if available, or a direct unit check of survey_patchwork on random tensors: output shape equal, values in [0,1], masked fraction of views ~ PATCH_P) before finishing.
